title: Electronic Health Record-Integrated Quality Dashboard for Diabetes Care in Public Primary Health Care: Development and Usability Study.
abstract:
Background

Quality dashboards are essential tools in health care, providing integrated and visualized data to support decision-making. Continuous monitoring of key indicators is crucial for managing chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus and improving outcomes.

Objective

This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interactive diabetes quality dashboard integrated within the public health care system of Tandil, Argentina, to support monitoring and decision-making in primary care.

Methods

A participatory and multidisciplinary approach was used to design and implement the dashboard. Development consisted of two phases: (1) indicator selection and visualization design and (2) dashboard development and iterative testing. This study was conducted between October 2024 and May 2025. Indicators were initially identified from national clinical practice guidelines and Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set standards and refined through 2 in-person workshops with 10 stakeholders (a health system decision-maker, primary care physicians, nurses, researchers, and IT specialists) who were purposively selected by the research team and local primary health care authorities based on their institutional role and involvement in diabetes care, chronic disease management, or health information systems and were personally invited to participate. Six virtual group sessions were then conducted with the same stakeholders to iteratively refine the dashboard based on their feedback. The dashboard was integrated into an existing electronic health record system and developed using Apache Superset. Usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale following an exploratory evaluation in which participants independently explored the dashboard without predefined tasks.

Results

Stakeholder workshops and iterative testing informed the dashboard's content and design. The final dashboard integrated 29 indicators across 6 tabs in 3 sections for population-level monitoring of adults with diabetes. Among 9 health care professionals participating in the usability assessment, the mean System Usability Scale score was 78.7 (SD 9.4), and 8 (88.9%) scored above the standard benchmark of 68. All participants considered the dashboard useful for health decision-making, 7 suggested further data disaggregation, and 3 recommended benchmarking capabilities.

Conclusions

The dashboard received favorable usability scores and may support population-level monitoring of diabetes care in public health settings. Its integration into an existing electronic health record system and participatory development were key strengths. Future research should assess its impact on care processes and clinical outcomes and explore its adaptation to other health care systems.

title: Developing a Stakeholder-Informed Quality Use of Medicines Analytics Dashboard for Acute Mental Health Care: Protocol for a Cross-Country Study.
abstract:
Background

Digital transformation of health systems is occurring and accelerating globally across both high-income and low- and middle-income countries, creating new opportunities for data-driven care improvement. Mental health conditions affect approximately 20% of the population in both Indonesia and Australia. Ensuring medicines are used safely and effectively, known as the quality use of medicines (QUM), is critical in mental health care, where treatment frequently involves long-term and potentially complex medication regimens.

Objective

This study aims to use electronic medical records (EMRs) in Indonesia and Australia to improve medicine use in acute mental health care and inform policy and practice, enabling shared learning across different health system contexts.

Methods

This study is being conducted in parallel across both countries from 2024 to 2026, comprising four phases: (1) identification, (2) reconciliation, (3) translation, and (4) validation. A co-design approach is being applied throughout, involving people with lived experience of mental illness, clinicians, policymakers, and health informaticians through focus groups and stakeholder consultations.

Results

This project was funded by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade through the Australia-Indonesia Knowledge Partnership Platform (KONEKSI) in June 2024, with project activities commencing in August 2024. To date, 2 clinician focus group meetings and consumer focus groups involving stakeholders across Australia and Indonesia have been completed. A scoping review examining QUM in acute mental health settings has also been completed. Findings from these activities have informed data mapping and the identification of preliminary dashboard indicators. Analysis of stakeholder consultation data has been completed, with dissemination activities currently underway. The project is currently progressing to dashboard development and refinement, with ongoing stakeholder engagement and knowledge translation activities planned to support future implementation and evaluation.

Conclusions

This study will contribute to public health by improving the safety, effectiveness, and equity of mental health care through enhanced medicines management. By developing stakeholder-informed, EMR-based, data-driven quality indicators and analytics tools, this study will support continuous quality improvement and generate transferable insights to inform policy and practice across diverse health systems.

title: NMA-KIT: An interactive knowledge translation tool for network meta-analysis to bridge evidence and practice.
abstract:
Objective

Network meta-analysis (NMA) is increasingly used to compare multiple interventions and inform clinical guidelines, health policy, and decision-making. However, inconsistent reporting and challenges in communicating complex findings can limit the accessibility, transparency, and practical application of NMA results. To address these challenges, we developed the NMA Knowledge Interactive Translation (NMA-KIT) tool, an interactive web-based application integrated within NMAstudio 2.0, to enable a seamless workflow from analysis to communication of results.

Study design and setting

The tool was developed to enable a seamless workflow from analysis to communication of results and was demonstrated using an exemplar NMA of systemic treatments for psoriasis.

Results

NMA-KIT provides a structured and user-friendly framework for communicating NMA findings. The Detailed Report enables in-depth exploration of treatment effects, underlying data, assumptions, and certainty of evidence, whereas the KIT Summary presents concise, clinically focused results. Additional functionalities include interactive data filtering, customizable visualizations, absolute risk estimation, access to study-level information, and collaborative project sharing.

Conclusion

NMA-KIT represents an important step forward for bridging the gap between NMA results and decision-making. By combining interactive visualization, flexible exploration, and integrated project sharing within NMAstudio 2.0, the tool has the potential to improve transparency, reproducibility, and communication, ultimately supporting more informed and collaborative evidence-based decisions.

title: Photon-Counting CT for Postoperative Imaging of Cochlear Implants: Comparison to Flat-Detector CT.
abstract:
Objectives

After FDA approval in 2021, photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCCT) has demonstrated its feasibility for high-resolution imaging while lowering the radiation dose at the same time. High-resolution visualization of cochlear implant (CI) integrity and positioning is crucial for postoperative management. The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of PCCT for postoperative imaging after CI implantation in comparison to high-resolution flat-detector CT (FDCT), the current clinical gold standard.

Materials and methods

Postoperative PCCT scans after cochlear implantation were retrospectively analyzed from August 2024 to April 2026. Scans were included for analysis if FDCT acquisition had been before PCCT on the same patient in the course of sequential bilateral cochlear implantation. Image quality was assessed in consensus by 2 experienced readers using a scoring system analyzing structural delineation of the inner and middle ear, CI integrity, metal and motion artifacts as well as calculating an overall score. Radiation dose was retrieved from the picture archiving and communication system.

Results

Twenty-eight postoperative PCCT scans of patients after CI implantation with a mean time delay of 4.5±5.1 years between FDCT and PCCT scans were evaluated. Image quality of PCCT was noninferior to FDCT for all single imaging features (P<0.001, eg, distinction of single CI electrodes: median [interquartile range] PCCT 3 [3 to 3]; FDCT 3 [3 to 3]; P<0.001) with the exception of the homogeneity of bony structures and the mastoid cell septation (P=0.999). PCCT was superior to FDCT in reducing metal and motion artifacts and increasing the delineation of the stapes (P=0.009 to <0.001; eg, metal artifacts PCCT 3 [2.75 to 3]; FDCT 2 [1 to 2]; P<0.001). Effective radiation dose of PCCT was 0.05±0.01 mSv and 8.8±5.4-times lower than for FDCT with 0.44±0.29 mSv (P<0.001) applying our institutional protocols.

Conclusions

Regarding image quality in postoperative assessment of CI, PCCT is noninferior to or in single features better than FDCT at a significantly lower radiation dose and shorter scan time.

title: Nerve-targeted Fluorophores for Intraoperative Facial Nerve Visualization: A Scoping Review of Translational Readiness and Evidence Gaps.
abstract:
Background

Iatrogenic facial nerve injury remains a major source of morbidity in head and neck and facial surgery, particularly when nerves are small, distorted, or chronically denervated. Nerve-targeted fluorophores may improve intraoperative visualization, but their translational readiness remains unclear.

Methods

A scoping review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through February 2026 for peer-reviewed studies evaluating fluorescence-based visualization of the facial nerve or facial nerve-relevant cranial/peripheral nerves. Study design, probe characteristics, quantitative imaging performance, workflow, safety, nerve state, and translational stage were synthesized descriptively.

Results

In total, 21 records met inclusion criteria, of which 19 were nonhuman and 2 involved humans, including 1 abstract-level feasibility study and 1 phase 1 trial. Probe strategies included peptide-dye platforms targeting nerve sheath/extracellular matrix, oxazine-based small molecules, paired-agent approaches, and myelin-directed myelin protein zero constructs. Reporting of contrast metrics and imaging workflows was heterogeneous. In a direct chronic denervation model, bevonescein produced a greater signal-to-background ratio than oxazine-4 (3.31 ± 1.11 versus 1.27 ± 0.54; P < 0.001). The phase 1 bevonescein trial demonstrated feasible dosing and timing, objective contrast enhancement, and no dose-limiting toxicities.

Conclusions

Nerve-targeted fluorescence demonstrates strong preclinical promise and early clinical feasibility, but evidence is insufficient for routine adoption. Future studies should standardize imaging metrics, stratify results by nerve state and target biology, and link improved visualization to operative safety, postoperative facial function, and patient-centered outcomes.

title: Career Trajectories and Role Differentiation among Master's-Level Health Informatics Graduates: A Mixed-Methods Workforce Analysis.
abstract:
Background

Health informatics (HI) is an evolving interdisciplinary field critical to modern healthcare delivery, requiring a workforce with advanced technical and analytical competencies. While prior studies have examined alignment between HI curricula and employer needs, limited research has explored actual career trajectories and role differentiation of HI graduates.

Objective

Examine career trajectories, role transitions, and factors influencing career progression among graduates of Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education [CAHIIM]-accredited master's-level HI programs.

Methods

A mixed-methods study was conducted using survey data from graduates (2017-2024) of CAHIIM-accredited HI programs. Quantitative analyses included descriptive statistics, Sankey visualization of career transitions, and multinomial logistic regression to assess predictors of role differentiation. Qualitative thematic analysis was performed to identify perceptions of degree value and employment experiences.

Results

Among 234 respondents, 179 reported 301 postgraduation jobs, with an average of 1.68 positions and a mean tenure of 2.82 years. The most common roles were "care processes and information technology integration" and "data analyst." Career pathways demonstrated domain stability and seemingly upward mobility, with transitions from technical roles to leadership positions. Employer sector was the strongest predictor of role differentiation, with payer and government sectors associated with leadership roles, while provider settings emphasized operational roles. Qualitative findings highlighted positive perceptions of degree value and challenges such as difficulty securing employment, employer preference for clinical credentials, and concerns about return on investment.

Conclusion

HI graduates follow structured yet varied career trajectories, typically entering technical roles and progressing to leadership positions over time. Employer sector significantly shapes career outcomes, while tenure alone is less predictive of advancement. Findings suggest insights valuable to educational institutions and organizations, including the need to integrate leadership skill development throughout the degree, stronger academic-industry alignment, involvement of industry personnel in curriculum development and instruction, enhanced internship and job placement support, and clearer articulation of HI competencies to optimize workforce readiness.

title: A New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene Radiological Incident Dashboard Design.
abstract: Public health specialists who must respond to a radiological emergency in jurisdictions using RadResponder to share a map of the measured radiation exposure rate data can be at a disadvantage unless they themselves or dedicated staff are familiar with the intricacies of the application. Even if that is the case, the RadResponder map is not public-health-focused and cannot easily display all or even most of the radiation readings simultaneously to provide public health leadership with an overview of the situation. A map that presents representative exposure rate data, perhaps augmented by a color code or other means to express the hazard level for non-radiation specialists like public health leads could serve as an alternative. Such a map could also be easier for the public to understand, especially if pertinent locations were highlighted such as schools, hospitals, daycare centers, and other familiar sites affected by the incident. Other data visuals that track operations associated with or under the direction of public health, such as Community Reception Centers, could be combined with the incident map into a dashboard useful for health department emergency operations center personnel to swiftly obtain situational awareness. This paper describes a prototype radiological incident dashboard developed for the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene.

title: pyGENIE: A Python library for programmatic access and mutational analysis of AACR Project GENIE.
abstract:
Motivation

As of today, AACR Project GENIE has completed 19 data releases since its launch in 2015. The latest release includes more than 268 000 samples from nearly 250 000 patients, and as of February 2026, over 1730 scientific journal articles have cited Project GENIE data. Despite its scale and scientific impact, programmatic analysis of GENIE data often still requires researchers to work directly with complex flat files and develop custom data integration workflows.

Results

Here we present pyGENIE, a Python package that provides a unified API for accessing GENIE flat files, performing clinical and genomic queries, computing tumor mutational burden, and integrating with leading mutational signature analysis tools including SigProfiler and SigMA. Following a data-as-a-service paradigm, pyGENIE returns all results as native pandas DataFrames, enabling seamless integration with machine learning and visualization libraries. Applied to a lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) case study, pyGENIE reproduces known mutation frequencies, co-mutation patterns, and mutational signatures while reducing the required codebase by approximately an order of magnitude.

Availability

pyGENIE is freely available at https://github.com/gersteinlab/pyGENIE under the MIT License, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21981945, and can be installed from PyPI using pip install pygenie-sdk.

Supplementary information

Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: An estimand framework to guide model and algorithm validation in predictive modelling.
abstract:
Background

Model validation is important to quantify the generalization capability of a predictive model or learning algorithm. In practice, data splitting is required to quantify the relevant out-of-sample performance reliably. For practitioners it is often unclear which of the available data splitting schemes is most suitable for their specific problem. This is particularly true when not only (in-distribution) reproducibility but also (out-of-distribution) transferability to another population or context needs to be assessed.

Methods

We performed a selective review to assess the documentation of external validations of clinical risk prediction models in the literature. We derived a novel estimand framework based on existing frameworks for treatment and diagnostic studies. To conduct statistical inference, we adopted different established methods for our purpose (exploratory visualization, three-level meta-analysis, Bayesian mixed model​). Finally, we applied our framework in a hypothetical predictive modelling study based on real-world data.

Results

Our new framework allows a precise specification of the relevant performance estimand by defining constraints on inference and development context. To facilitate practical application, we provide an algorithm which allows estimand-aligned data splitting. We also propose a novel structured nested cross-validation scheme to enable an adequate empirical comparison of reproducibility and transferability. Our numerical experiments illustrate that the estimand can influence empirical validation results and should thus be carefully chosen. The meta-analysis approach offers a good compromise between simplicity and suitability for comparing the performance corresponding to different estimands.

Conclusion

Our framework facilitates the specification of the estimand in the predictive modelling context and thus helps to describe the validation gap between validation study and intended use more precisely. It can improve the current practice in the clinical risk prediction literature where the estimand is often only vaguely defined and the usefulness of the performance estimate(s) is thus unclear.

title: Communicating dermatologic drug safety: a comparative evaluation of United States and United Kingdom pharmacovigilance systems using dapsone as a model medication.
abstract:
Purpose

Postmarketing pharmacovigilance systems are essential for identifying adverse drug reactions (ADRs) that may not be recognized during premarketing clinical trials. Although the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS) and the United Kingdom Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) Yellow Card Scheme share the common objective of medication safety surveillance, little is known about how these systems differ in organizing and communicating postmarketing safety information to clinicians. This study compared the clinician-facing organization, accessibility, and communication of postmarketing safety information between the FDA AEMS Public Dashboard and the MHRA Yellow Card Interactive Drug Analysis Profile (iDAP) using dapsone as a representative dermatologic medication.

Methods

A cross-sectional comparative pharmacovigilance study was conducted using publicly available FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card data extracted on June 29, 2026. Descriptive analyses characterized adverse-event reports, patient demographics, clinical outcomes, MedDRA Preferred Terms, and System Organ Class distributions. The two pharmacovigilance platforms were qualitatively compared using a predefined framework assessing data accessibility, organization, clinical usability, and research utility.

Results

The FDA AEMS identified 4,793 reports associated with dapsone-containing products, including 3,686 (76.9%) classified as serious and 280 (5.8%) reporting death. The MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identified 699 reports comprising 1,701 adverse reactions, including 559 (80.0%) serious reports and 25 (3.6%) fatal outcomes. Both systems demonstrated overlapping patterns of reported adverse reactions. Despite similar pharmacovigilance outputs, substantial differences were observed in the communication of safety information. The FDA emphasized downloadable datasets, customizable searches, and case-level transparency to facilitate secondary pharmacovigilance analyses, whereas the MHRA prioritized standardized, drug-specific summaries, hierarchical MedDRA organization, integrated visualizations, and contextual guidance to support rapid clinical interpretation.

Conclusions

The FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identify similar postmarketing safety profiles for dapsone while employing distinct approaches to communicating pharmacovigilance information. These complementary strengths suggest that future clinician-facing pharmacovigilance platforms should integrate the analytical flexibility of the FDA with the standardized, medication-specific communication strategies of the MHRA to improve the translation of postmarketing safety data into dermatology practice while preserving scientific transparency.

title: Predictive Model for Early Identification of Poor Prognosis in Kidney Transplant Recipients Based on Ultrasound Hemodynamic Parameters Combined with Clinical and Laboratory Indicators: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
Objectives

This study aimed to identify kidney transplant recipients with functioning grafts at the 3-month post-transplant who were at high risk of subsequent adverse graft outcomes. We developed predictive models and nomograms integrating ultrasound hemodynamic, clinical, and laboratory parameters.

Methods

We analyzed 376 kidney transplant recipients enrolled from January 2020 to April 2023. The 2020-2022 cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n = 200) and an internal random holdout set (validation set 1; n = 131). The subsequently enrolled 2023 cohort was retained as the temporal validation set (validation set 2; n = 45). All ultrasound predictors were assessed at the approximately 3-month post-transplant. Risk factors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression. Predictive models were constructed using logistic regression and 5 machine-learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and a nomogram was developed for visualization. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the machine-learning models.

Results

The final logistic regression model included graft renal segmental artery resistance index (Grsa RI), preoperative albumin, and postoperative day 5 platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (Po5 PLR). Its AUCs were 0.893 in the internal random holdout set (validation set 1) and 0.859 in the temporal validation set (validation set 2). The random forest model, selected on the basis of the highest training-set AUC among the machine-learning models, achieved AUCs of 0.916 and 0.821 in validation sets 1 and 2, respectively. DeLong tests showed no statistically significant difference in AUC between the logistic regression and random forest models in either validation cohort (p = .958 and p = .561, respectively). Preoperative albumin, Po5 PLR, and Grsa RI were independently associated with adverse graft outcomes.

Conclusions

The prediction models effectively identified high-risk recipients using pre- and postoperative variables, providing an actionable strategy for early intervention to improve transplant outcomes by targeting modifiable factors.

title: Eye-Tracking Use for Assessment and Rehabilitation of Driver Performance: A Scoping Review.
abstract: BackgroundDriving rehabilitation increasingly incorporates eye tracking to quantify visual-cognitive performance; however, its clinical relevance and patterns of use remain unclear.PurposeThis scoping review maps how eye-tracking technologies, metrics, and applications are used in driving assessment and rehabilitation, and characterizes the populations studied.MethodFollowing Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR, five databases were searched (January 2001-July 2026). Thirty-nine eligible studies were charted for population, driving task, eye-tracking metrics, and device type.FindingsStudy populations included older adults (24 studies), autism spectrum disorder (5), traumatic brain injury (3), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (3), visual field impairment (3), and stroke (1). Eye tracking was applied to hazard perception, visual exploration and scanning, visual-motor coordination, and cognitive workload. Simulator studies mostly used remote screen- or dashboard-mounted systems, whereas on-road studies mostly used head-mounted systems. Drivers in several populations showed delayed first fixation on hazards, fewer fixations on relevant targets, and narrower or spatially biased visual search than comparison drivers.ConclusionThese population-specific gaze signatures indicate that eye tracking offers an ecologically relevant complement to occupational therapy driving assessment. Normative gaze datasets, standardized reporting, and validated clinical thresholds are needed before eye-movement metrics can guide routine return-to-drive decisions.

title: ADCdb 2.0: clinical landscape and ADMET profiles of antibody-drug conjugates.
abstract: Systematically characterizing antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) is essential for understanding their therapeutic properties, guiding molecular design, and supporting clinical development. Recently, the expanding clinical landscape of ADCs has generated extensive information on target antigens, therapeutic indications, and clinical trial pipelines, providing a valuable foundation for informing ADC development strategies. Moreover, ADMET profiles are critical for understanding the in vivo disposition, efficacy, and safety of ADCs. Integrating these accumulating clinical and pharmacological data is therefore necessary to enrich the evidence available for ADC development. In this study, ADCdb was updated to provide (i) detailed clinical landscape information for 542 ADCs, together with >3000 manually curated clinical trials from registries across nine registries and clinical trial platforms; (ii) >4000 ADMET profiles, including quantitative pharmacokinetic parameters and descriptive annotations supported by relevant references; and (iii) expanded pharmacological information and biological activity data comprising 13 088 ADC entries and 24 821 activity records, as well as ADC-specific functional annotations for 389 ADCs. Interactive visualization tools and antigen- and disease-centered search modules further enable systematic exploration of ADC composition, therapeutic indications, and clinical development. ADCdb 2.0 is expected to serve as a valuable resource for rational optimization of ADCs, and is accessible at https://idrblab.org/adcdb/.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Natural Products: Potential Effects on Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism in Heart Failure.
abstract:
Background

Heart failure (HF), the end-stage of cardiovascular disease (CVD), affects over 64 million people globally. There is an alarming trend of earlier onset, which poses a substantial healthcare burden. Although guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has significantly improved clinical outcomes, residual morbidity and mortality remain considerable, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial energy metabolism (MEM) plays an important role in HF pathophysiology and represents a potential therapeutic target. Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived natural products (TCM-derived NPs) contain diverse bioactive constituents that may influence myocardial energy metabolism and related pathological processes, warranting further investigation into their potential role in HF management.

Purpose

This review aims to synthesize current evidence on the involvement of MEM in HF and the potential regulatory effects of TCM-derived NPs. It further integrates mechanistic evidence with exploratory network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to identify candidate compound-target relationships and discuss their translational implications.

Methods

The following keywords were used: "heart failure," "traditional Chinese medicine," "ATP synthesis," "oxidative phosphorylation," "fatty acid oxidation," "glucose metabolism," "mitochondrial membrane potential," "reactive oxygen species," "energy metabolism," "mitochondrial dynamics," "calcium signaling," and "energy coupling." Potential targets of NPs were obtained from the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform. We collected disease-related targets from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, GeneCards, and the Therapeutic Target Database. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis was performed using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID). Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using STRING and analyzed in Cytoscape 3.10.0 to identify candidate hub genes. Ten representative bioactive compounds were separately examined through exploratory molecular docking with the candidate hub proteins.

Results

Herb-frequency analysis of 132 clinical studies identified 15 high-frequency Chinese medicinal herbs for subsequent computational analysis. The literature synthesis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), fatty acid and glucose metabolism as key processes involved in myocardial energetic remodeling in HF. Separately, KEGG enrichment analysis identified pathways related to metabolic regulation, cellular stress, and inflammation, including lipid and atherosclerosis, PI3K-Akt, HIF-1, insulin, and TNF signaling pathways. PPI analysis prioritized AKT1, JUN, TP53, MAPK1, and MAPK3 in the MEM-related network and STAT3, TNF, TP53, IL6, and ESR1 in the inflammation-metabolism crosstalk network, yielding nine unique candidate hub genes after deduplication. Molecular docking of ten representative bioactive compounds with these nine candidate proteins yielded predicted docking scores ranging from -4.5 to -9.7kcal/mol.

Conclusion

The available evidence supports MEM as an important component of HF pathophysiology and suggests that selected TCM-derived NPs may influence multiple MEM-related processes relevant to HF. By integrating mechanistic, clinical, and computational evidence, this review provides a structured framework for understanding NPs-MEM-HF relationships and offers a basis for future mechanistic validation and clinical translation.

title: Reliability-Aware Morphology-Based Automated Platelet Analysis for Identification of CBC Unreliability From Peripheral Blood Smear Images.
abstract: Platelet evaluation plays a critical role in the diagnosis and clinical management of thrombocytopenia. Although automated hematology analyzers allow rapid platelet estimation, their accuracy can be compromised in the presence of abnormal platelet morphology, particularly in cases of aggregation and pseudothrombocytopenia, necessitating peripheral blood smear examination, which increases manual workload and reliance on subjective interpretation. This study presents a morphology-centric framework for automated platelet analysis from peripheral blood smear images, with a focus on assessing the reliability of automated interpretations. A pilot dataset of 200 Leishman-stained smear images acquired at x1000 magnification was categorized into normal, hypoproductive, hyperdestructive, and platelet clump-dominant classes. Image preprocessing and segmentation techniques were applied to identify platelet regions and extract morphology-based parameters, including platelet count, mean platelet area, size variation, and aggregate presence. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences among platelet classes (p < 0.001), and association testing confirmed a strong relationship between platelet morphology and clumping patterns. A rule-based interpretation strategy was implemented to identify smear conditions likely to produce unreliable complete blood count (CBC), whereas a lightweight convolutional neural network was employed to examine learnable morphological patterns, achieving approximately 85% test accuracy, with visualization confirming that the model attended to relevant platelet regions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of incorporating morphology-guided reliability assessment into automated platelet analysis and provide a foundation for future validation on larger clinical datasets.

title: One-Step Rectified Flow Reconstruction with Spectral Weighting for Limited-angle Cardiac CT.
abstract: Limited-angle cardiac computed tomography (CT) suffers from severe directional artifacts and resolution degradation due to missing wedges in the frequency domain. Diffusion-based reconstruction methods have demonstrated strong artifact suppression capabilities but typically require iterative sampling at a high computational cost. To accelerate limited-angle CT reconstruction, we propose a rectified-flow framework trained with paired supervision for fast inference. Instead of generating images from Gaussian noise, the model learns a deterministic transport from artifact-contaminated Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions to full-view reference images. A 2.5D slice-context modeling strategy is introduced to exploit inter-slice information while reconstructing only the central slice, improving structural consistency. Furthermore, we introduce a reconstruction-aware spectral loss that applies frequency-domain supervision to an approximate endpoint reconstruction inferred from the predicted flow velocity. By embedding spectral priors into the learning objective and using one-step rectified-flow inference (a single network evaluation), the proposed framework achieves fast reconstruction while preserving image fidelity. Experiments on XCAT simulations and clinical cardiac CT data show superior quantitative performance and substantially reduced inference time compared to the state-of-the-art baselines. A qualitative review by an experienced cardiac radiologist further suggests improved visualization of motion-sensitive coronary structures with reduced motion blur.

title: High-depth whole-genome sequencing of blood culture plates reveals evolutionary dynamics in cases of persistent bacteremia due to methicillin-resistant <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i>.
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) can be applied to clinical cultures to detect polyclonal variation within a single bacterial strain, enabling the tracking of within-host evolution and transmission. Culture isolates from infected patients are often sequenced as individual colonies (c-seq). To increase the sensitivity of variant detection, cultures can also be sequenced as a pool (p-seq), but the utility of this approach is not clear for most clinical specimens. To understand how these methods perform in bacteremia, we applied p-seq to blood culture plates for 10 patients with persistent bacteremia due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. For comparison, we also applied c-seq to five colonies (c5-seq) from the same plates for six patients. p-seq was more sensitive than c5-seq for detecting low-frequency variant alleles; however, the most important factor for new variant detection was the number of culture plates analyzed, rather than the sequencing method used. We also used these data to construct Muller plots for three patients with especially diverse infecting populations, enabling the visualization of rapid evolutionary dynamics in response to antibiotic exposures. We identified 204 unique variant alleles, and our analysis provides additional evidence for parallel evolution of several different genes during S. aureus bacteremia, including genes linked to antibiotic evasion (rpoB and vraS), metabolism (pdxK), energy production (qoxA), and virulence (saeS). Overall, these data provide a detailed view of evolutionary dynamics during clinical cases of MRSA bacteremia and describe the merits and limitations of c-seq vs p-seq strategies for analyzing blood culture plates using WGS.IMPORTANCEAs bacterial whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used as a research tool for clinical samples, it is important to understand the pros and cons of different culture sampling methodologies. Here, we analyzed cases of persistent bacteremia due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) by applying WGS of either five individual colonies isolated on blood culture plates (c5-seq) or the pooled bacterial population on each plate (p-seq). We found that p-seq was more sensitive for allele detection, but that c5-seq was better suited to understand evolutionary dynamics. Our analysis also provided evidence for the evolution of specific genetic loci of MRSA that are involved in antibiotic evasion, metabolism, energy production, and virulence. Finally, examination of patient-level factors suggests prosthetic valve endocarditis and severe immunosuppression may be risk factors for polyclonal bacteremia.

title: Development and In-Vitro Validation of the First Functional, Patient Specific, Metal Additively Manufactured Aneurysm Clip.
abstract:
Objective

Recent aneurysm clip improvements enhance biocompatibility and imaging artifacts through new materials, while design remained limited. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of 3D printing aneurysm clips, including the development of the first functional, patient-specific, metal 3D-printed clip.

Methods

A 5.8 mm wide case of unruptured intracranial aneurysm previously treated with aneurysm ligation through clipping was included, and a complete imaging dataset acquired and segmented. One standard and one patient-specific clip design were evaluated using a Finite Element Model (FEM) simulation to assess clip blade dimensions with respect to the aneurysm sac. Metal 3D printing was employed to produce the clip blades, then assembled with standard clip springs. The produced prototypes were then tested on a silicone 3D-printed physical simulator under exoscope visualization and indocyanine green angiography in a neurosurgical laboratory. Occlusion of the implanted patient-specific clip was then assessed using CT imaging.

Results

The FEM simulations confirmed design adequacy, with the patient-specific design reducing maximum strain and stress than the standard design respectively of 4.3% and 14%. Both 3D-printed clip designs presented self-occluding functionality, with a maximum dimensional deviation of 90 μm, and a tip-to-tip aperture capacity reduced from 9 mm of traditional clips to 7 mm and 6 mm, respectively. The 3D-printed clips fully occluded the silicone aneurysm sac. The patient-specific design avoided dog-ear formation and improved vascular reconstruction, then radiologically confirmed.

Conclusions

Metal 3D printing enabled the first self-closing, patient-specific aneurysm clip, with functional feasibility demonstrated in a simulated setting; comprehensive mechanical characterization is the next step toward clinical application.

title: Development of PRECISE, a Data-Driven Personalized Suicide Prevention Intervention: Protocol for an Intervention Refinement Pilot and Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
Background

Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STBs) are heterogeneous in their causes and course, yet most interventions rely on nomothetic, one-size-fits-all models. Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) is an evidence-based treatment for STBs, but its standard year-long format is resource-intensive and difficult to access. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) combined with idiographic (person-specific) statistical modeling offers a way to identify which emotion regulation processes are driving an individual's risk, and in turn to select the DBT skills most relevant for that person.

Objective

This protocol describes the refinement (aim 1) and preliminary evaluation (aim 2) of PRECISE (Personalized Clinical Intervention for Suicidal Events), an 8-week, EMA-informed, idiographically tailored adjunctive treatment for adults with active suicidal ideation.

Methods

In aim 1, an existing PRECISE treatment manual and clinician dashboard will be iteratively refined with a mentorship and advisory panel and tested for feasibility and acceptability in a small, randomized pilot study (n=10; n=5 per arm), comparing high- and low-intensity personalization schedules. In aim 2, 60 adults with active suicidal ideation will be randomized to a high-intensity (weekly idiographic model updates across all 8 EMA-monitored weeks) or low-intensity (single idiographic model generated after an initial 2-week EMA burst) version of PRECISE. Both arms will receive coach-delivered DBT skills selected according to each participant's idiographic model, which will be generated using the group iterative multiple model estimation (GIMME) algorithm. Primary outcomes include usability, retention, EMA adherence, acceptability, and fidelity; secondary and exploratory analyses will examine trajectories of suicidal ideation and a within-person mediation model linking emotion regulation to STBs.

Results

The trial registration record (ClinicalTrials.gov) was first posted on February 5, 2025, and enrollment began on November 14, 2025. The study is currently recruiting. Estimated total enrollment across aim 1 and aim 2 is 70 participants. Primary and final data collection are anticipated to be complete by March 2030. The study was funded in May 2025, and data collection began in November 2025. As of November 9, 2026, 7 participants had been enrolled. Results are expected to be published in approximately the beginning of 2030.

Conclusions

PRECISE is, to our knowledge, the first idiographically personalized, EMA-informed adjunctive treatment developed specifically for STBs. This trial will provide feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy data to inform a subsequent fully powered efficacy trial.

title: Development and validation of the health literacy-sensitive pharmacist-patient communication scale.
abstract:
Introduction

Health literacy is central to healthcare quality, and clinical pharmacists play a crucial role in improving patients' health literacy and medication safety. China, however, lacks a locally validated tool for evaluating health literacy-sensitive pharmacist-patient communication (HL-SPPC).

Objective

This study aims to develop and validate an evaluation indicator system and a patient self-assessment scale for HL-SPPC in Chinese inpatient pharmaceutical care.

Methods

An initial indicator pool was generated through a systematic literature review and focus group discussion and refined through two rounds of modified Delphi consultation; indicator weights were determined using the precedence chart method. A cross-sectional survey of inpatients who had received medication guidance from clinical pharmacists was conducted to evaluate psychometric properties, including item analysis, content validity, reliability, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity.

Results

The final indicator system comprised 5 primaries and 19 secondary indicators, with the higher weights for visualization and tool support (36%), communication strategies (28%), and feedback responsiveness (20%). The validated 11-item patient scale yielded two factors, empathic communication (7 items) and concrete guidance (4 items), which explained 68.827% of the total variance. The overall Cronbach's α was 0.859, and the test-retest ICC (2,1) was 0.710. Confirmatory factor analysis indicated acceptable fit (χ²/df = 1.779, CFI = 0.959, TLI = 0.947, RMSEA = 0.080, SRMR = 0.045). Convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity were acceptable.

Conclusion

This study provides the first validated indicator system and patient self-assessment scale for HL-SPPC in China, offering practical tools for pharmacist training, pharmaceutical care quality evaluation, and patient engagement.

title: Ross procedure through hemisternotomy.
abstract: Ministernotomy is not a common approach in aortic root surgery. However, in our opinion, during the Ross procedure, and considering certain anthropometric parameters and the presence of an experienced aortic team, ministernotomy is a convenient approach for adequate visualization of the structures of the right ventricle outflow tract and the aortic root. Our team presents a successful clinical case of surgical treatment of a 24-year-old patient with a bicuspid aortic valve, annuloaortic ectasia (aortic annulus diameter of 30 mm) and grade 3 aortic regurgitation. In this specific clinical case, we demonstrate the step-by-step Ross procedure using ministernotomy.

title: Application of augmented reality in frame-based stereotactic brain biopsy: a case series feasibility study.
abstract:
Purpose

Frame-based stereotactic biopsy (STB) lacks intraoperative visual control. Augmented reality (AR) via Microsoft HoloLens 2 offers real-time visualization of the biopsy needle. This study evaluates the technical feasibility and preliminary clinical results of AR navigation during standard frame-based STB.

Methods

This prospective single-center pilot study included 10 adults undergoing STB for intracranial lesions. Standard trajectory planning utilized the Cosman-Roberts-Wells (CRW®) stereotactic frame, intraoperative computed tomography (CT), and preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in NeuroSight Arc®. Concurrently, Medgital software and HoloLens 2 displayed a hologram of the patient's head, lesion, and trajectory. A passive tracker on the biopsy needle enabled real-time holographic visualization. Endpoints included technical feasibility, registration time, navigation error, diagnostic yield, and complications.

Results

AR navigation feasibility was confirmed in all 10 patients (100%). Mean registration time was 79 ± 27 s, and mean AR trajectory error relative to standard planning was 2.21 ± 0.67 mm. A definitive histological diagnosis was obtained in all 10 cases (mean passes: 2.4). No hemorrhagic complications or mortality occurred.

Conclusion

Integrating AR navigation (HoloLens 2 and Medgital) with conventional frame-based STB is potentially technically feasible, safe, fast, and provides acceptable accuracy. AR complements the standard workflow by offering direct intraoperative visualization of the needle trajectory.

title: A Point-of-Care Integrated Detection System for Rapid Mycobacterium leprae Detection Using RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a and Lateral Flow Assay.
abstract:
Objectives

Leprosy remains a significant public health challenge in many regions, and inadequate point-of-care (POC) diagnostics often delay treatment and lead to disability. We aimed to establish an optimized RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a POC system for M. leprae detection with integrated reagents, equipment and colloidal gold visualization.

Methods

The workflow comprised 1 min of tissue DNA release, 15 min of incubation and amplification in the instrument, and approximately 16 min for CRISPR detection. Assay conditions were optimized (200 nM primers, 37°C, 100 nM each of Cas12a and crRNA), and analytical sensitivity and specificity against non-leprosy mycobacteria were evaluated. Clinical performance was assessed in 219 clinical samples and compared with Ziehl-Neelsen staining and PCR.

Results

The detection limit was 100 copy/μL for M. leprae DNA, with no cross-reactivity with other mycobacteria. Among 179 confirmed leprosy samples, CRISPR-Cas12a detected all multibacillary (MB) samples (100%) and 65.21% of paucibacillary (PB) cases, outperforming PCR (39.13%) and acid-fast staining (0%) and comparable to qPCR (63.04%). All non-leprosy samples were negative by CRISPR-Cas12a.

Conclusions

This POC-compatible platform holds promise for early diagnosis, and the integrated reagents and equipment further enhance convenience for on-site testing in resource-limited settings, supporting timely intervention and leprosy control efforts.

title: How I do… endoscopic breast revision surgery.
abstract: Breast implant reconstruction is widely used but is associated with complications in approximately 30% of cases, with capsular contracture being the most common. Its incidence increases substantially after radiotherapy and may lead to aesthetic deformity, pain, and revision surgery. This article describes a minimally invasive endoscopic approach to breast revision surgery, including capsulotomy and capsulectomy. The technique is performed through a small incision placed away from the implant pocket, preferably using a pre-existing axillary or inframammary scar. A single-port device provides access for endoscopic instruments, while insufflation at 10 mmHg improves operative exposure and facilitates identification of capsular retractions. The main advantages of this approach are improved surgical ergonomics, enhanced visualization, precise dissection, and effective hemostasis. Endoscopic visualization also facilitates surgical education by allowing the entire operating team to follow the procedure. Implant insertion can be performed using a Keller Funnel®-type sleeve, enabling a no-touch technique. The procedure takes approximately 40 minutes and can generally be performed on an outpatient basis. Postoperative complications remain similar to those of conventional surgery, including hematoma, seroma, and prosthetic infection. Endoscopic revision surgery is a promising alternative to conventional surgery, particularly for minimizing scars near the implant. However, its clinical benefits and potential reduction in complications require confirmation through larger cohort studies.

title: Comparison of ocular radiation doses between ultra-low-dose photon-counting computed tomography and digital radiography for orbital foreign body screening: A phantom study.
abstract:
Introduction

Metallic orbital foreign bodies may pose a safety risk during magnetic resonance imaging due to potential displacement or heating of ferromagnetic material within the magnetic field, potentially resulting in severe ocular injury. When their presence cannot be reliably excluded based on patient history, imaging is performed as a precautionary screening step prior to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Digital radiography (DR) is commonly used for this purpose due to its low radiation dose but provides limited anatomical and spatial information. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high spatial resolution and improved dose efficiency and may serve as an alternative ultra-low-dose screening technique. This phantom study compared radiation exposure between DR and ultra-low-dose PCCT for orbital imaging.

Methods

Orbital imaging was performed in an Alderson RANDO phantom using DR and PCCT. Absorbed radiation doses to the eye lens and globe were measured using optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters (OSLDs) and effective doses were estimated from standard dose descriptors and compared for both modalities.

Results

Mean absorbed doses of PCCT imaging were 0.092 mGy for the lens and 0.087 mGy for the globe, compared with 6.215 mGy and 4.855 mGy for DR, corresponding to dose reductions of 98.5% and 98.2%. Effective doses were 0.002 mSv for PCCT and 0.023 mSv for DR, corresponding to a 91.3% reduction.

Conclusion

Ultra-low-dose PCCT substantially reduced ocular radiation exposure compared with DR while allowing visualization of the tested metallic foreign body. Further studies are warranted to evaluate its diagnostic performance as a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body screening prior to MRI.

Implication for practice

Ultra-low-dose PCCT may represent a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body imaging prior to MRI, with the additional benefit of cross-sectional visualization. Further validation of diagnostic performance is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: SPARC: sectorized partial-angle reconstruction based motion correction method for multi-phase CCTA.
abstract: Objective.Multi-phase coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides a clear visualization of coronary arteries, offering comprehensive and reliable imaging support for the clinical diagnosis of coronary artery disease. However, traditional motion correction reconstruction algorithms lack reconstruction robustness despite their interpretability, while deep learning reconstruction methods achieve high imaging quality at the expense of interpretability and anatomical reliability in clinical CCTA practice. This study aims to simultaneously achieve interpretable and robust multi-phase coronary reconstruction.Approach.We propose a motion trajectory estimation and motion correction framework termed sectorized partial-angle reconstruction-based motion correction (SPARC) for CCTA. The proposed framework integrates sectorized partial-angle reconstructions, a spatio-temporal cascaded network for coronary centerline extraction, and a phase-accumulated fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm for motion trajectory estimation. These components work together to minimize motion estimation errors and enhance the quality of motion-corrected reconstruction.Main results. Experimental results from both simulations and clinical studies demonstrate that SPARC achieves superior reconstruction performance compared with existing methods. SPARC effectively reduces coronary motion artifacts and restores clear vessel structures while preserving reconstruction fidelity, achieving the best scores on all metrics.Significance.By preserving both interpretability and anatomical reliability while effectively reducing motion artifacts, SPARC provides a clinically deployable solution for motion-corrected multi-phase CCTA, supporting more reliable imaging for coronary artery disease diagnosis.

title: Accuracy of Cone-beam Computed Tomography in Determining Implant Length and Diameter: A Comparative Clinical Evaluation.
abstract:
Background

Accurate preoperative assessment of implant dimensions is a critical determinant of success in dental implant therapy. Precise estimation of implant length and diameter helps avoid complications such as cortical plate perforation, inferior alveolar nerve injury, and inadequate primary stability. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has become an important imaging modality in implant dentistry because it provides three-dimensional visualization with relatively low radiation exposure compared to conventional computed tomography.

Aim

The study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of CBCT in determining implant length and diameter by comparing radiographic measurements with actual implant dimensions used during surgery.

Study design and setting

This was a prospective, comparative clinical study conducted in a dental teaching hospital.

Subjects and methods

Patients requiring dental implant placement were included in the study. Preoperative CBCT scans were obtained, and measurements of proposed implant length and diameter were recorded using dedicated CBCT software. During implant placement, the actual implant length and diameter used were documented. Radiographic measurements obtained from CBCT were then compared with the clinical implant dimensions.

Results

CBCT measurements showed a high degree of agreement with the actual implant length and diameter used during surgery. Minor discrepancies were observed, but these differences were within clinically acceptable limits. CBCT demonstrated high accuracy in preoperative assessment of implant dimensions.

Conclusion

CBCT is a reliable and accurate imaging modality for determining implant length and diameter. Its use in preoperative planning can enhance surgical safety and improve the clinical outcomes in dental implant therapy.

title: Comparison of Laryngeal Mask Airway Protector and Intubating Laryngeal Mask Airway for Ease of Fiber-optic-guided Tracheal Intubation in Adult Patients: A 1-year Hospital-based Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
Background

Supraglottic airway devices (SADs) have become integral to modern airway management, particularly in difficult airway scenarios and fiber-optic-guided tracheal intubation. The intubating laryngeal mask airway has long been regarded as a reliable conduit for tracheal intubation, whereas the LMA Protector™, a newer second-generation SAD, offers additional advantages including improved airway sealing and gastric drainage channels. Comparative evidence regarding their efficacy as conduits for fiber-optic-guided intubation remains limited.

Objectives

The objective of this study was to compare the ease of fiber-optic-guided tracheal intubation through the LMA Protector and Intubating LMA and to evaluate the grade of glottic view obtained through both devices using a flexible fibrescope.

Materials and methods

This randomized controlled trial was conducted at KLES Dr. Prabhakar Kore Charitable Hospital and Medical Research Centre, Belagavi, over a period of 1 year. Sixty-eight patients aged 20-60 years belonging to the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grades I-III and undergoing elective surgeries under general anesthesia were enrolled and randomized into two groups of 34 each. Group I underwent intubation using Intubating LMA, whereas Group P underwent intubation using LMA Protector. Parameters assessed included time taken for LMA insertion, grade of resistance during insertion, number of insertion attempts, time taken for tracheal intubation, number of intubation attempts, and grade of glottic view obtained with fiber-optic bronchoscopy.

Results

The demographic characteristics and ASA grading were comparable between the two groups. Mean time taken for LMA insertion was 27.36 ± 2.73 s in Group I and 29.17 ± 2.02 s in Group P, with no statistically significant difference (P = 0.188). First-attempt LMA insertion success was achieved in 91.2% of Group I and 88.2% of Group P patients (P = 0.690). Tracheal intubation time was significantly shorter in Group I compared to Group P. Both devices demonstrated high overall success rates for fiber-optic-guided intubation and satisfactory glottic visualization.

Conclusion

Both the Intubating LMA and LMA Protector were effective conduits for fiber-optic-guided tracheal intubation with high success rates and comparable ease of insertion. The Intubating LMA demonstrated a shorter intubation time, whereas the LMA Protector provided comparable glottic visualization and insertion characteristics. Operator familiarity and clinical context remain important determinants in device selection.

title: Seeing deeper, seeing more: Complementary philosophy in the constructions of fluorescence imaging probes for surgical navigation.
abstract: Optical imaging offers a powerful visualization modality for precise intraoperative navigation. The core of intraoperative navigation lies in reliably distinguishing lesions from surrounding normal tissues during surgery. For optical imaging, this translates to endowing target tissues with a sufficient signal-to-background ratio (SBR, which is generally considered to be ≥5). However, most existing studies focus on optimizing performance within a single spectral window, either near-infrared (NIR) or visible light, while overlooking the inherent complementarity of the two in clinical scenarios. This review returns to the central issue of intraoperative navigation and systematically summarizes the research progress of NIR and visible-light imaging in probe design, imaging window expansion, and luminescence modes. NIR imaging, through background suppression arising from low tissue scattering, low autofluorescence, and moderate light absorption, enables the localization and recognition of deep tissues ("seeing deeper"). In contrast, visible-light imaging, owing to its high compatibility with the surgeon's naked-eye white-light field of view, is well suited for guidance and execution in superficial surgical fields ("seeing more"). Accordingly, we propose two complementary intraoperative navigation modes: NIR fluorescence empowering intelligent surgical robots, and visible-light fluorescence assisting direct operation by surgeons. On this basis, we further discuss frontier directions including dual-band synergistic systems, multimodal theranostic integration, and intelligent surgical decision-making, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation and design inspiration for the construction of next-generation intraoperative navigation strategies.

title: Ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction in pediatric intussusception: focus on the frond sign and immobility.
abstract:
Background

Ultrasonography-guided hydrostatic reduction permits real-time visualization of pediatric intussusception, but the sonographic appearance of the residual intussusceptum at the endpoint of failed reduction has not been well characterized.

Objective

To characterize ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction and to explore their relationships with operative findings.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study included 234 pediatric cases treated with ultrasonography-guided hydrostatic reduction between December 2005 and January 2026. Clinical characteristics were compared between successful and failed reductions. In failed cases, intussusception mobility during reduction and final ultrasonographic findings of the irreducible intussusceptum, including the frond sign and trapped fluid, were assessed. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used.

Results

Of 234 cases, 216 (92%) were successfully reduced and 18 (8%) failed. Patients in the failed group were younger and had longer symptom duration (P<0.001 and P=0.002, respectively). Among failed cases, 14 (78%) intussusceptions were mobile and 4 (22%) were immobile. Immobility was associated with bowel resection (P=0.01), and both ileocolocolic cases were immobile. The frond sign was present in 13 cases (72%) and was more frequent in mobile than immobile cases (P=0.02). Trapped fluid was present in 14 cases (78%) but was not associated with mobility or operative method.

Conclusion

Final ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction may help characterize the residual intussusceptum. The frond sign was common, whereas persistent immobility was associated with bowel resection and was observed in both ileocolocolic cases.

title: FAP-targeted molecular imaging of CAFs-mediated chemoresistance and reversal by JAK/STAT inhibition in gastric cancer.
abstract: Chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle in the clinical management of gastric cancer (GC), driven largely by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). CAFs activate the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in GC cells, promoting proliferation, migration, and resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), highly expressed on CAFs but minimally in normal tissues, is an attractive target for molecular imaging. Here, we developed FAPtp-ICG, a near-infrared fluorescent probe comprising an FAP-targeting peptide conjugated to indocyanine green (ICG), for noninvasive visualization of FAP expression. We established CAFs-conditioned GC models with graded chemoresistance, in which FAP-associated fluorescence and FAP expression were positively associated with the degree of CAFs-mediated 5-FU resistance in the experimental models. FAPtp-ICG enabled noninvasive fluorescence imaging of FAP-associated stromal changes, allowing longitudinal assessment of treatment-associated changes related to CAFs-mediated drug resistance. Mechanistically, combination therapy with 5-FU and ruxolitinib (RUX) suppressed JAK/STAT signaling, alleviated chemoresistance, inhibited tumor growth, and restored drug sensitivity. Multi-omics profiling further revealed that RUX treatment was associated with transcriptomic and proteomic alterations in the tumor microenvironment, attenuating inflammatory signaling, immune cell recruitment, and extracellular matrix remodeling. By integrating a FAP-targeted optical probe with therapeutic JAK/STAT inhibition, this work demonstrates a theranostic strategy for assessing and overcoming CAFs-mediated chemoresistance in GC, supporting the potential utility of FAP-targeted imaging for longitudinal assessment of treatment-associated stromal changes.

title: Whole-body fetal 3D CINE MRI with low flip angle balanced steady-state free precession acquisition within the specific absorption rate limit at 1.5 T.
abstract:
Purpose

To develop a three-dimensional (3D) CINE magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequence for assessing whole-body fetal movements within the specific absorption rate (SAR) limit, and to evaluate its clinical feasibility.

Methods

A 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) CINE MRI sequence was developed at 1.5 T within a whole-body averaged SAR of ≤ 2 W/kg. Half-scan artifacts (zero-valued pixels) and flip angle (FA) effects on signal intensity and contrast were assessed in phantoms. Seventeen fetal examinations (14 with the final protocol) were evaluated visually by two readers and by the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between fetal tissues and amniotic fluid.

Results

Zero-valued pixels appeared with the half-scan technique and increased as the half-scan factor decreased. The contrast between the phantoms was greater at higher FAs. Reducing the FA to 25° allowed a shorter TR within the SAR limit, enabling a 3D slab placed over the fetus to be acquired without the half-scan technique at a temporal resolution of approximately 320 msec (whole-body SAR, 1.59-1.94 W/kg). The CNRs between the amniotic fluid and the brain, lung, abdomen and limbs were 24.1 ± 10.6, 23.1 ± 12.8, 27.3 ± 14.3 and 30.9 ± 9.2, respectively. With the final protocol, both readers identified fetal movement in 11 of 14 examinations (κ = 1.00), and fold-over artifacts impaired the evaluation in two and three examinations, respectively.

Conclusion

Low-FA 3D bSSFP CINE MRI at 1.5 T enables visualization of whole-body fetal movements within the SAR limit at a temporal resolution of approximately 320 msec.

title: Robotic-Assisted Uterus Transplantation: A Cadaveric Feasibility Model.
abstract:
Objective

To study the feasibility of robotic-assisted uterine allograft implantation in a human cadaveric model, addressing the technically demanding vascular anastomoses required for living-donor uterus transplantation. Over the past two decades, uterus transplantation (UTx) has progressed from preclinical studies through early clinical trials and into clinical practice (1-3). It remains the only therapeutic option for individuals with absolute uterine-factor infertility to carry their own pregnancy (4, 5). During early clinical trials, both living donor graft procurement and recipient implantation were performed exclusively via open laparotomy (1, 6, 7). Since that time, minimally invasive surgical approaches have been serially adapted to minimize donor surgical morbidity and take advantage of the superior 3D visualization and wristed instrumentation of the robotic platform (2, 5). Although robotic-assisted techniques have become well adapted and standardized for living donor hysterectomy at high-volume centers (4, 5), recipient implantation has received less development and remains predominantly performed through an open approach (2). Building upon the established success of robotic approaches in solid organ transplantation, such as robotic kidney transplantation, we aim to adapt these microsurgical techniques to recipient uterus transplantation.

Design

Narrated, stepwise video of robotic implantation of a uterine graft in a cadaveric model using the da Vinci platform. This study was performed using a human cadaveric donor. Use of the donated body for research and educational purposes was authorized through the institution's body donation program in accordance with institutional policies and applicable regulations.

Subjects

A uterine graft procured through an organ procurement organization from a 50-year-old brain-dead donor, implanted in a 67-year-old female cadaver in an academic cadaver laboratory.

Exposure

Robotic-assisted uterus transplantation. The graft was benched to replicate a living-donor procurement, using only the anterior division of the internal iliac artery and taking the ovarian and inferior uterine veins without a venous patch, yielding six small-caliber vessels. After perfusion with histidine-tryptophan-ketoglutarate solution, each vessel was spatulated cranially and marked for orientation. Through a Pfannenstiel incision, four robotic arms were docked, and the recipient external iliac artery and vein were dissected bilaterally. Six vascular anastomoses were performed end-to-side to the external iliac vessels with running 7-0 Prolene, and the vaginal anastomosis with running 3-0 barbed suture.

Main outcome measures

Total console time, time for each vascular anastomosis, need for anastomotic revision, and technical patency of the anastomoses on inspection after graft removal.

Results

Total console time was 156 minutes. Individual anastomosis times ranged from 11 to 14 minutes; no anastomosis required revision. After graft removal, all anastomoses were inspected and confirmed technically patent.

Conclusion

Robotic-assisted implantation of a uterine graft is technically feasible in a cadaveric model. This robotic approach may offer a minimally invasive approach to uterus transplantation; further preclinical and clinical studies are warranted.

title: Designing the Bipolar Action Network: A Learning Health Network to Improve Outcomes for People Living With Bipolar Disorder.
abstract: The U.S. system of care for people with bipolar disorder is fragmented, and population-level outcomes have not improved in two decades. To address this gap, the authors have designed and developed the Bipolar Action Network, a Learning Health Network (LHN) in which people with lived experience, clinicians, researchers, and health system leaders collaborate to improve care through shared data, coproduction, and continuous quality improvement (QI). Using a structured idealized system design process, the design team articulated a shared purpose, mapped current systems, surfaced existing evidence and innovations, and developed a theory of change. The team selected an initial portfolio of system-change interventions spanning leadership, clinical care, technology, and learning. Seventeen health systems and 86 individuals participated in the design phase. The network developed governance documents, a single institutional review board protocol, a measurement framework, a dashboard, and an online knowledge repository. Eight care centers completed QI training during the design; five of the nine pilot projects achieved measurable improvements in care processes. The design process demonstrates that a structured, participatory design can produce a functioning LHN with the leadership, infrastructure, and improvement capacity to transform care for patients with complex psychiatric conditions.

title: Caregiver-Informed Safety and System Requirements for Real-Time Feedback During Pediatric Inhaler Use: Qualitative Concept-Elicitation Study.
abstract:
Background

Correct use of a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI), usually with a valved holding chamber, depends on use-related conditions that caregivers may not observe directly, including inhalation pattern, actuation-inhalation timing, mask seal, and device orientation. Many digital inhaler systems emphasize actuation or adherence. Systems that infer technique-related conditions from proxy signals may add real-time feedback but also create false reassurance if a positive state is displayed when evidence is inadequate. Caregiver expectations for such feedback and its failure states remain poorly characterized before prototype development.

Objective

This study aimed to characterize caregivers' experiences of pediatric inhaler administration and translate responses to a proposed sensor concept into traceable candidate safety, system, and validation requirements.

Methods

We conducted 23 semistructured concept-elicitation sessions through Zoom videoconference with 27 caregivers of children who currently or previously used a pMDI. Interviews consisted of 19 individual and 4 dyadic sessions pairing 2 caregivers from different households. Sessions were conducted remotely between April and July 2026 from the University of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Recruitment originated in Calgary and was not geographically restricted. A 6-phase guide examined current practices, difficulties, prior digital-tool use, and responses to a screen-shared clip-on concept incorporating airflow-, timing-, seal-, and orientation-related sensing; on-device feedback; an optional child-facing app; and a caregiver dashboard. No working prototype was evaluated. Approximately 86,000 transcript words underwent hybrid directed and conventional qualitative content analysis using an 18-category codebook. Two researchers independently coded the complete 27×18 matrix (486 paired decisions) across 2 rounds. Consensus categories were translated into candidate requirements and assigned an earliest verification or evaluation locus. Counts are descriptive caregiver-voice tallies, not prevalence estimates.

Results

Persistent uncertainty about whether administration conditions were adequate was the dominant lived experience (19/27); for 5 caregivers, existing passive cues had not resolved it. A simple, real-time on-device signal was endorsed by 25 caregivers, but willingness to consider the concept was conditional on reliability (9 caregivers named reasons for abandonment, notably a "false green"), low-friction operation during acute symptoms (12/27), minimal added bulk and technique change, and one or more of clinical validation, clinician recommendation, or a trial pathway (composite category; 23/27). Stances on gamification (20/27), dashboard cadence (18/27), aesthetics (24/27), and privacy (18/27) supported an optional, configurable software layer. Intercoder agreement was 94% (Cohen κ=0.88). The analytic synthesis yielded a conceptual architecture separating observable proxy signals, an inference and data-quality gate, and positive, corrective, or uncertain feedback states.

Conclusions

Participating caregivers prioritized immediate and interpretable feedback about use-related conditions. The findings support conservative state assignment, an explicit uncertain state for indeterminate signals, and app-independent acute-use feedback. These are candidate requirements rather than validated device specifications; subsequent work should proceed through bench verification, simulated-use human factors evaluation, and prospective clinical or field validation.

title: Benchmarking in Medication Safety: A Report from the Alliance of Dedicated Cancer Centers Patient Safety Organization.
abstract: Benchmarking is commonly used in health care to compare performance among providers. However, medication safety has largely been exempt from this type of benchmarking: using voluntarily reported medication safety events for cross-institutional performance comparisons is discouraged because these data are not directly comparable. The member hospitals of the Alliance of Dedicated Cancer Centers (ADCC) launched a Patient Safety Organization (PSO)-supported Medication Quality and Safety Dashboard project to examine whether this cohort was similar enough that benchmarking could illuminate medication safety vulnerabilities and best practices. In this retrospective analysis, the authors evaluated institutional demographics, pharmacy volume metrics, and deidentified medication safety event reports from existing systems; developed a severity crosswalk; standardized key event definitions; normalized event rates per 10,000 doses dispensed or administered; and calculated a near-miss event (NME) ratio as a marker of reporting culture. Despite these efforts, the study revealed that heterogeneity in reporting platforms, system configurations, data capture practices, and institutional size produced wide variability and significant outliers in event volumes and rates, precluding meaningful cross-institutional performance comparisons. The authors' findings reaffirm long-standing cautions against benchmarking voluntarily reported event data across institutions, even among seemingly similar cancer centers. However, they found practical value from internal use of the NME ratio to assess reporting culture and error interception, and from collaborative work to standardize taxonomy for medication safety events that goes beyond the medication-use phase and medication type. They identified best practices for using internal medication-related safety data. These lessons can be applied to the incorporation of AI as more tools and literature support become available.
